items.title: Turkey engaging all sides to end Iran war, foreign minister says

featured_image.name: Turkey says it's engaging with all sides to end Iran war ...

items.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Tuesday condemned the ongoing US-Israeli military offensive against Iran as a "clear violation" of international law and vowed to intensify diplomatic efforts to secure a ceasefire, as the conflict that began on February 28 showed no signs of abating.

items.title: Merz meets Trump as Germany's military buildup reshapes Europe

featured_image.name: Trump, Germany's Merz build ties in friendly meeting on ...

items.description: As German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met with President Donald Trump at the White House on March 3, the visit underscored a striking transformation: Germany, long defined by post-war pacifism, is racing to build Europe's most powerful conventional military force. The ambition has drawn cautious applause from allies — but also quiet anxiety in capitals from Paris to Warsaw about what a heavily armed Germany means for the balance of power on the continent.

items.title: Survey finds one in three European women face violence

featured_image.name: One in three EU women face violence, most cases unreported ...

items.description:
Roughly one in three women in the European Union have experienced physical or sexual violence in their lifetime, yet the vast majority of cases are never reported to authorities, according to a sweeping new survey released on March 3 by the EU Agency for Fundamental Rights and the European Institute for Gender Equality.[1][2]

The report, titled "EU Gender-based Violence Survey: Evidence for Policy and Practice," draws on interviews with more than 114,000 women aged 18 to 74 conducted between September 2020 and March 2024 across all 27 member states. It found that 30.7% of women reported having experienced physical violence, threats, or sexual violence by any perpetrator — a figure that represents a slight decline from the 33% recorded in the inaugural survey conducted in 2012.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's Assembly of Experts elects Mojtaba Khamenei as next supreme leader

featured_image.name: Son of Iranian Regime's Supreme Leader Suspends Religious ...

items.description:
Iran's Assembly of Experts has elected Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as the next leader of the Islamic Republic under pressure from the Revolutionary Guards, according to Iran International, citing informed sources. The reported selection, which has not been officially confirmed by Iranian state media, came even as Israeli airstrikes struck the very building where the clerical body had gathered to count votes in the holy city of Qom.[1][2][3]

The unconfirmed appointment would mark a dramatic and controversial hereditary transfer of power in a republic whose theocratic system has never before passed the supreme leadership from father to son.

items.title: Iran threatens to attack any ship in Strait of Hormuz as Asia scrambles for energy

featured_image.name: Oil supertanker rates hit all-time high as insurers drop war risk protection in the Middle East

items.description:
Asian governments and energy companies are racing to secure alternative oil and gas supplies as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz following U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran threatens to choke off the region's most critical energy artery. With Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps officials declaring the strait "closed" and warning that any vessel attempting to pass would be attacked, the world's most oil-dependent economies face their most serious supply disruption in decades.[1]

The strait, a narrow passage between Iran and Oman, typically carries roughly 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas. An estimated 84% of crude oil and 83% of LNG transiting the waterway is destined for Asian markets, with China, India, Japan, and South Korea accounting for an estimated 69% of oil and 59% of LNG flows.[2][3]

items.title: Syria deploys thousands of troops to Lebanon border

featured_image.name: Syria sends thousands of troops to Lebanon border, sources ...

items.description: Syria has reinforced its border with Lebanon by deploying thousands of soldiers, rocket units, and armored vehicles, according to a Reuters report citing eight Syrian and Lebanese sources. The buildup began in February but accelerated in recent days as hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah intensified across the region.[1]

featured_image.name: Senate confirms Air Force veteran Dan Caine as Joint Chiefs ...

items.description: The United States and Israel launched a massive coordinated military assault against Iran on February 28, 2026, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior officials in an operation that has plunged the Middle East into its most serious conflict in decades. Now entering its fourth day, the war has drawn in Gulf Arab states through Iranian retaliatory strikes and sparked fierce international debate over its legality and endgame.

items.title: Afreximbank raises Caribbean financing cap to $5B

featured_image.name: Afreximbank to establish its largest HQ at Egypt's new ...

items.description: The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) has increased its financing ceiling for the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) from $3 billion to $5 billion, marking the latest expansion of economic ties between Africa and the Caribbean diaspora.

items.title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of drone attacks in its civil war

featured_image.name: Sudan implicates Ethiopia in its civil war

items.description:
Sudan's army-backed government has formally accused Ethiopia of allowing drones to be launched from its territory to strike targets inside Sudan, marking the first time Khartoum has directly implicated its neighbor in the nearly three-year-old civil war.[1][2]

In a statement issued Monday, March 2, the Sudanese Foreign Ministry said the government had been "monitoring, throughout February and into early March, the ongoing unauthorized entry of unmanned aircraft (drones) from inside Ethiopian territory into Sudanese airspace, targeting locations within Sudan". The ministry described the incursions as "a flagrant violation of Sudan's sovereignty and a clear act of aggression against the Sudanese state".[3][4][1]

The statement did not specify who carried out the attacks, how many occurred, or which locations were hit. However, according to Reuters, the southeastern Blue Nile state, which borders Ethiopia, has seen small skirmishes and drone attacks in recent weeks. Parts of Blue Nile are controlled by the SPLM-N rebel group, which aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces last year.[5][1]

items.title: Israel says it destroyed secret Iranian nuclear site near Tehran

featured_image.name: Israel hit nuke weapons research site in Iran last month ...

items.description:
The Israeli military announced on Tuesday that its air force destroyed a secret Iranian nuclear weapons development facility on the outskirts of Tehran, marking the first public acknowledgment that Iran had begun rebuilding weapons capabilities dismantled during last year's 12-day war.

IDF Chief Spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin identified the partially underground facility as "Min Zadai," located on the northeast outskirts of the Iranian capital. According to the IDF, a group of nuclear scientists had been "working secretly to develop capabilities required for nuclear weapons" at the compound. Israeli intelligence tracked the scientists as they attempted to travel to the site clandestinely, ultimately revealing the nature of the work being conducted there.[1][2][3]

items.title: Macron orders evacuations, deploys forces as Iran conflict strands hundreds of thousands

featured_image.name: Macron says European powers to offer Iran a diplomatic exit ...

items.description: Governments across Europe scrambled on Tuesday to repatriate hundreds of thousands of their citizens stranded in the Middle East, as widespread airspace closures triggered by the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran left travelers and residents unable to return home.

items.title: Iranian drone strikes US Consulate in Dubai as war widens across Gulf

featured_image.name: Iranian drones strike U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia as war ...

items.description:
A drone struck the parking area of the US Consulate in Dubai late Tuesday, igniting a fire that was quickly extinguished by emergency teams, as Iran's retaliatory campaign against American interests across the Gulf expanded into its fourth day following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

No casualties were reported, according to both a US official and Dubai's government media office. Videos geolocated to the consulate showed dark smoke rising from near the compound. The attack came as Iran continued to unleash projectiles on the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states in retaliation for the US-Israeli military operation that began February 28.[1][2][3]

items.title: Macron deploys aircraft carrier to Mediterranean amid Middle East crisis

featured_image.name: France sending aircraft carrier to Mediterranean, Macron ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron announced on Tuesday the deployment of France's nuclear-powered aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle to the Mediterranean, marking a major European military escalation as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran enters its fourth day. In a televised address from the Élysée Palace, Macron said the carrier, along with its Rafale fighter jets, air defense systems, airborne radar, and escorting frigates, had been ordered to leave its exercises in the North Atlantic and Baltic Sea and sail south immediately.[1][2]

"Confronted with this volatile environment and the unpredictability of the days ahead, I have commanded the aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle, along with its air resources and frigate escort, to embark for the Mediterranean," Macron said.[1]

items.title: Ukraine refuses EU requests to inspect damaged Druzhba pipeline

featured_image.name: EU 'would welcome' Ukraine repairing Druzhba pipeline to ...

items.description: The European Union is stepping up pressure on Ukraine to permit independent inspection of the Druzhba oil pipeline, which has been out of service since a Russian strike on January 27 disrupted the flow of crude to Hungary and Slovakia. Kyiv has repeatedly refused access requests on security grounds, fueling a dispute that has stalled a €90 billion EU aid package for Ukraine.

items.title: Trump to review military escorts, insurance for Hormuz tankers

featured_image.name: ‘It’s about time’: Trump says he will join gathering of US military leaders

items.description:
The Trump administration is actively considering deploying naval escorts for oil and gas tankers traversing the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S.-Iran conflict threatens to choke off a waterway responsible for roughly 20 percent of global crude and gas shipments, according to multiple reports on Tuesday.

"Military support for oil and gas supplies," a person familiar with the discussions told Politico. "It's becoming a growing concern that the energy markets could face pressures in the coming days as the military campaign intensifies and expands in geographic scope. Access to the Straits of Hormuz is obviously vital for both natural gas and crude oil shipments, especially from Qatar and Saudi."[1]

items.title: SpaceX's Starship faces 5-month launch gap as IPO filing nears

featured_image.name: SpaceX's major Starship test delayed after technical issue

items.description:
SpaceX has gone nearly five months without a Starship launch — the longest pause since the program's early days — even as the company prepares to file paperwork for what could become the largest initial public offering in history.

The world's largest rocket last flew on October 13, 2025, when Flight 11 closed out a year of five test missions. As of early March, no official launch date has been set for Flight 12, and the mission does not appear on SpaceX's online schedule. Elon Musk suggested in a January 26 post on X that the next launch was six weeks away, pointing to a March liftoff, but that timeline has not been confirmed by the company.[1][2][3]

items.title: Apple unveils six devices in two days, more expected

featured_image.name: Apple MacBook Pro M5 14-inch review: A huge graphics ...

items.description:
Apple has announced six new products over two days in its most aggressive spring launch in years, with at least one more device expected when the company hosts media at a hands-on "experience" event on Wednesday.

The announcements began Monday, March 2, with the iPhone 17e and the M4 iPad Air, followed Tuesday by the M5 MacBook Air, M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro, and a pair of new Studio Displays. Pre-orders for most of the new hardware open March 4, with availability beginning March 11.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Dow sinks as oil surges on Iran's Strait of Hormuz shutdown

featured_image.name: Iran partially closes Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil choke point, as Tehran holds talks with U.S.

items.description:
Oil prices soared for a third consecutive day on Tuesday and stocks tumbled sharply as the war between the United States and Iran entered its fourth day, with tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz at a near standstill and no signs of a quick resolution to the conflict.

West Texas Intermediate crude climbed roughly 8% to around $76.91 per barrel, while Brent crude jumped about 7.6% to $83.65, its highest level since mid-2024, according to CNN. The Dow Jones Industrial Average sank more than 1,000 points in early trading, while the S&P 500 fell over 2% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped by a similar margin.[1][2][3]

items.title: Indian team hits 30.2% efficiency in perovskite-silicon solar cell

featured_image.name: Perovskite solar cells maintain 95% of power conversion ...

items.description: A wave of recent breakthroughs in perovskite solar cell research is bringing the promising but fragile technology closer to commercial viability, with teams across Asia and Europe reporting new methods to boost both efficiency and long-term stability in tandem perovskite-silicon devices.
